_schema: IDENTITY of the 2000-prompt real-benign sample the published nano false-positive figure is measured on. It carries SHA-256 hashes of the prompt texts and NOT the texts themselves: no_robots is CC-BY-NC-4.0 and cannot be redistributed from an Apache-2.0 repository, and a hash is not the work. `scripts/intent_metrics.py --real-benign` rebuilds the sample by downloading the three public datasets, hashing every candidate prompt and selecting the ones named here, so the published figure is reproducible by a stranger without this repository shipping anyone else's licensed text. WHY A FIXED SAMPLE AND NOT A FRESH DRAW: this one was assembled for the model-acceptance battery and is disjoint from the sets the model was selected and calibrated against; a freshly drawn sample is not, and measuring on prompts the model was tuned against biases the false-positive rate downward. A fresh draw at the same size and seed overlaps this sample by 128 of 2000 and reads 33/2000 rather than 37/2000 for that reason.
method: Sources: databricks/databricks-dolly-15k `instruction` (CC-BY-SA-3.0); HuggingFaceH4/no_robots data/train_sft first user turn (CC-BY-NC-4.0); OpenAssistant/oasst1 data/train English first-turn prompter messages, not deleted (Apache-2.0). Each text is .strip()ed before hashing. Candidate filter: at least 4 words (nano's own gate) and fewer than 20000 characters.
hash: sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the stripped prompt text
duplicate_note: The sample contains one prompt twice ('What is orange wine?', which appears twice in dolly-15k). It is recorded here with count 2 rather than deduped, because the published figure is the number the acceptance battery measured and silently changing the sample would change it.
published_figure: 37/2000 = 1.85%, Wilson 95% [1.35%, 2.54%], measured through the shipped sensor with enable_nano=True at the shipped operating point (NANO_T_OP 0.0079) on xaidr 1.7.0 + onnxruntime 1.29.0. Reproduce with: python scripts/intent_metrics.py --nano --real-benign
